definitions.gloss: browsing without intending to buy; window-shopping
definitions.explanation: Looking over goods in a shop or stall with no intention of buying. Often used by shopkeepers of customers who take up their time.
Making fun of someone in a light or mocking way, especially calling out remarks from the sidelines.

examples.japanese: {買|か}う{気|き}はなく、ただの{冷|ひ}やかしだった。
examples.english: I had no intention of buying; I was just browsing.

examples.japanese: {屋台|やたい}の{店主|てんしゅ}は、{冷|ひ}やかしの{客|きゃく}にも{笑顔|えがお}で{応|おう}じていた。
examples.english: The stall owner responded with a smile even to customers who were only browsing.

examples.japanese: {客席|きゃくせき}から{冷|ひ}やかしの{声|こえ}が{飛|と}んだ。
examples.english: Jeering voices came from the audience.

examples.japanese: {二人|ふたり}が{付|つ}き{合|あ}い{始|はじ}めたと{知|し}って、{同僚|どうりょう}たちの{冷|ひ}やかしが{止|と}まらなかった。
examples.english: Once word got out that the two had started dating, their colleagues wouldn't stop teasing them.

notes:
The noun form of {冷|ひ}やかす (to tease; to browse without buying). The shopping sense is the more common one in everyday signs and speech.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {冷|ひ}やかしお{断|ことわ}り: no browsers (sign at stalls and shops)
- {冷|ひ}やかしの{客|きゃく}: a customer who is only looking
- {冷|ひ}やかし{半分|はんぶん}: half in jest
- {冷|ひ}やかしの{声|こえ}: jeering, teasing remarks

SIMILAR WORDS:
- からかい: teasing — general playful mockery, without the shopping sense
- {見|み}るだけ: just looking — the neutral, polite way a customer describes browsing
